If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.

Ingredients:

6 tablespoons unsalted butter

1/2 cup white sugar

1/2 cup brown sugar

1/4 cup water

1/4 teaspoon cinnamon

1 pinch salt

5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced

1 pastry for double-crust pie

Directions:

Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.

Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.

Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.

Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.

Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Not gonna lie this game goes pretty damn hard overall for an early-access game. It's got a steep learning curve, a fun collection of weapons, and some really chaotic game-play when multiplayer gets involved. I've got a few main points to raise about the game so far, and I'll update this review if anything major changes about these things, but overall this game is really scratching my looty-shooty rogue-like itch. This game is gold, and it's worth the $10 price as it stands right now. If it ever goes on sale I'm likely gonna buy it for some friends who might like this, and I definitely hope I see more streamers playing this too.

• The graphics are solid and straightforward to the point of having very few symbols/items to confuse, though the descriptions and texts do force you to pause if only to read up all the info in a somewhat-small window. Plenty of room for improvement here, but the bones are ROCK SOLID and very fun to tinker with mechanically so I'm quite alright with pausing to check my build often.

• The UI could definitely be tightened up in the future, after Noisestorm gets their game-play loop and balance issues sorted, and when it does it'll really make the rest of this game pop.

• I love the feel of raw power creep with every upgrade I grab, and grabbing choice perks such as Driller and Green Dice at even level one can start to show immediate returns.

• YOU CAN PICK BAD PERKS FOR YOUR CURRENT WEAPON! This is GOOD! It means that perks aren't balanced around every weapon, and that BUILDS MATTER when choosing to use the crossbow vs the dual pistols. That being said I hope that in the future there are more options for damage, because right now MANY damage upgrades that come out of the chest have the chance to throw-off a weapon's performance. It's not so bad on the 'bullet-based' weapons but the weapons like the Cluster Launcher, Blade Launcher, and Orb Launcher can get a bit 'unique'.

• Sound design and quality are CHONKY and that only gets more-evident in multiplayer, the Cluster launcher feels *M E A T Y*, and I love the way the blade launcher's blades whoosh (slightly) as they fly. I don't expect to hear a lot more depth to sound in the mix with this game but I really don't feel like it needs much more to tell me everything I need to know in the fighting.

I personally call it Crab Game, but Crab Champions is a breath of fresh air compared to your typical AAA money grab that's constantly being pumped out year by year. For an early access game, I'm honestly impressed, yes they're some bugs here and there, but they go unnoticed and are an afterthought compared to the endless fun I'm having each playthrough. $14 honestly isn't enough. All the game lacks is more content, and from what the devs have teased, I can't wait. My buddy and I have been playing co-op lately and man I gotta say, this game has more replay capability than a Call of Duty game. 

This game further proves that AAA publishers are out of touch and that developers need to be free. Just look at what indie games have been doing compared to AAA studios. It's no longer about who can make the most photo realistic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, developers need to start making more passion projects and publishers need to back off and give them time. Crab Champions is amazing along with indie developers. They're the gifts that keep on giving, but most of all, they're the heroes we didn't deserve but desperately needed. In this money-hungry saturated industry that desperately needs change, I wish them nothing but success. this actually felt like a game and I really enjoyed it. Money well spent :)

This game was designed by someone who hates gamers. NONE of the enemies feel good to fight against, be it annoying trash mobs who spawn directly under you and instantly deal melee damage, or the elite enemies who are disgusting projectile dispensers. 

There is not a projectile in this game that escapes F tier design, they are all either fast and very hard to see with amazing predictive aim, or are huge, in great number, explosive, bouncing and leave aoe on the ground. The worst part of it all is that you dont even get to do that yourself most of the time, with the balance of the game seemingly centered around the player resetting repeatedly until they get a god build faster than they encounter one of the more heinously designed enemies.

UPDATE: Nearly a year on since I last updated this review, and I still mostly agree with what I previously wrote. I've gotten better at the game and have diamond on a handful of weapons. The good ones, that is, many weapons and abilities are basically useless. Some weapons start powerful, and others have features that help them scale well into the late game, but many are boring and/or suck and there's another option that fits the same nitch but performs way better.

Beyond your equipment is how your progress your character, mods. MANY mods are mediocre, and a bunch are just bad. As you gain time in this game you'll notice there's a small handful of common (not the rarity, but rate of acquisition) mods that really do anything for a build, and anything build defining or otherwise useful is exceptionally rare. Forget your ability and melee as damage options, as they hardly scale well past the first quarter of the run without complete dedication and a ton of luck to get one of the aforementioned rare mods (provided you are using one that's even worth picking in the first place)

Now, for the thing that really kills the game for me, the enemies. Perhaps the game got better, or maybe it was me, but my opinion of melee and explosive enemies has transformed from "they are bad like the rest" to meh. They work, they aren't so overwhelming or pestering like I previously though. My opinion of the ranged enemies, however, is more or less identical. Ranged enemies are very annoying: high projectile speed, predictive aim, high volume of projectiles, fire rate... I could go on, but I already said it all in the first review. Bullet hell games can be fun, but in a highly reflex based third person shooter with limitation/imprecision of movement, where you oftentimes cant see all the enemies or projectiles they spam at any given time? Not a fan, personally.

Many of the systems in this game are compelling on their surface and with minimal exposure, but sort of degrade as you go. The loadout system, for example, is cool, many weapons and abilities that can be mixed around, but eventually rou realized how many are bad or made redundant by a better weapon that does the same thing. The mod system too, is cool, but then you realize how many mods you ignore or never get to see. This game can be great fun, but oftentimes harsh rng or overtuned enemies get in the way of it.

I'm running out of things to say without sounding even more of a whiner, so I'll just wrap my review up by saying this game has a very solid foundation, but what was built upon it is in some places shakey.
